memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So God was kind to the midwives and the people increased and became even more numerous. And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families of their own." - Exodus 1:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the quiet reward. These women protected other people's babies, and God gave them households of their own. What they risked everything to defend in others, God multiplied to them.

We must be careful how we read this. This is not a formula — obey God and receive exactly what you want. Scripture is full of faithful people who died without seeing their reward (Heb 11:36-39). God is not a machine that dispenses blessings for good behaviour.

What this verse does tell us is something better: God notices. Nothing done in the fear of God escapes His attention, and He is generous by nature. Sometimes the reward comes in this life. Sometimes it waits for the next. But it never disappears.

Jesus said that not even a cup of cold water given in His name loses its reward (Mt 10:42). Your quiet obedience — the temptation refused, the truth told at cost, the person protected when it was easier to look away — is being recorded by a God who is kind.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I obey God for reward, or because He is worthy?
2. Where might God be asking me to do good without any recognition?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Kind Father, thank You that nothing done for You is ever wasted. Keep my heart faithful whether or not I see the reward. Amen.
